pages.text: WRITE puts a value into the I/O blocks as a variable item.

An expression follows and ends with $(1);$(). Each bound I/O block with an uninitialized variable item in its input gets the value. The item moves into the output and now holds the value. Its name is the name of the variable, like $(1)count$() for $(1)WRITE count ;$(). For any other expression, the name is $(1)output$().
If no bound I/O block has an uninitialized variable item, the cursor waits until a player puts one in. Laptops and tablets don't take part in WRITE.
Craft a NOOP block and an ink sac together.
The first line makes an item named $(1)count$(), the second one an item named $(1)output$().
